text:
micah: Heads-up — saw a sustained exporter CPU spike and p99 token latency climb after 03:10 UTC. Looks correlated with a handful of high-churn customers sending thousands of tiny spans. Not sure if this is batching or serializer lock contention.

opsbot: [ALERT] exporter-cpu-high service=telemetry-exporter p99_cpu=92% triggered at 2103456745

jordan: I captured a flame trace during the spike. Lots of time in exporter.SerialBuffer.flush and protobuf.Serialize. Small spans -> many tiny payloads -> flush hotloop.

jordan: log paste:
```
2026-03-19T03:12:10Z exporter.go:243 CPU=91% SerialBuffer.flush duration=1.2ms items=3
2026-03-19T03:12:11Z exporter.go:243 CPU=93% SerialBuffer.flush duration=1.8ms items=2
stack: exporter.SerialBuffer.flush -> protobuf.Marshal -> bytes.Copy -> sync.Mutex.Lock
```

rachel: ugh. That matches the retention TTL churn we saw from that mobile SDK. They batch <=3 spans per request. Batching window is 50ms by default, so frequent flushes.

sam: Can we raise batching window or enable coalescing for that route? We could apply a routing policy: for sdk/mobile-route, override exporter.batch_ms=200 and max_batch_items=256. Might increase tail latency but reduce CPU.

micah: We should be careful — increasing batch_ms globally will harm low-latency paths (realtime chat). Need route-level override and a canary rollout. Also want to ensure p99_token_latency per-route is surfaced in the console before rollout.

jordan: Quick repro curl to simulate small spans:
```bash
for i in {1..1000}; do curl -s -X POST https://telemetry.internal/v1/spans -d '{"spans":[{"name":"tick","duration_ms":1}]}' &
done
wait
```
This reproduces CPU spike in ~30s.

rachel: Dashboard idea: add a stacked view: exporter_cpu% by route, p99_ingest_latency by route, avg_spans_per_payload. Add a histogram of spans-per-request to find these mobile SDKs.

sam: Also consider softer mitigations: enable small-payload coalescing in the collector (hold 10ms extra for <8 spans) or increase serializer worker count. But more workers -> memory + GC cost.

micah: Priorities: 1) create a per-route dashboard panel (p99 + avg spans/payload) 2) canary a config change for sdk/mobile-route to batch_ms=200 and max_batch=128 3) if CPU persists, add route-level sampling for spans <10ms 4) measure unit economics (tokens/cost) and rollback plan.

jordan: I can wire up the dashboard tiles and a PromQL: sum by(route) (rate(process_cpu_seconds_total{component="exporter"}[1m])) and histogram for spans_per_payload_bucket.

opsbot: deploy-bot: starting canary for telemetry-exporter on pool=canary-telemetry (change: batch_ms=200) — job 2367

rachel: :eyes: monitoring p99_ingest_latency and exporter_cpu for canary-only traffic. If exporter_cpu > 80% or p99 > 500ms we abort.

sam: Quick config snippet for route override (collector-config.yaml):
```yaml
routes:
  - match: "sdk/mobile"
    exporter:
      batch_ms: 200
      max_batch_items: 128
      coalesce_small: true
```

micah: Good. Also add a trace sample to check that coalescing doesn't reorder spans incorrectly — we need stable ordering per-span parent.

jordan: After canary we saw exporter_cpu drop ~55% for that route and avg_spans_per_payload went from 2.1 -> 47. p99_ingest_latency increased from 120ms -> 170ms for that route but end-to-end app metrics unchanged. Can we promote?

rachel: Promote with conservative rollout: 10% -> 30% -> 100% over 15m steps, watch exporter_cpu and p99 per-route. Also add regression alert on quality metrics (missing-attrs, trace-drop-rate).

sam: Follow-ups: 1) follow-up eval to see if protobuf.Marshal is the hotspot (consider switching to faster codec or pre-serialized payload) 2) add per-route token quotas to prevent noisy tenants from causing fleet-wide CPU cost.

micah: I'll open an RFC for route-level quotas + console UX for per-route batching controls. Action items: jordan: dashboard + canary run notes; sam: code changes for coalescing; rachel: rollout plan and alerts; micah: RFC.

jordan: noted. Will paste dashboard links and canary metrics in this thread once ready.

opsbot: [INFO] job 2367 canary completed at 2103456829 status=success

micah: closing for now. Thanks all. Follow-up RFC link in #eng-platform when ready. :thumbsup:
